CSHL lets qualifying not-for-profits obtain CALs on a per-user basis for non-Windows servers such as SQL Server 2008, Internet Security and Acceleration (ISA) Server, and others. CSHL generally requires a minimum purchase of five licenses. Check out the Microsoft Licensing and Donation Program page for details about CSHL. CSHL licenses don't work for Windows clients (for example, Windows Server 2008) or devices. See previous sections for information about acquiring those types of client licenses.

How do you perform the OLST?
Have the patient start with their eyes closed.3 Then have the patient slowly raise their hands up along their sides until both of their arms are fully extended at their sides. Next, with the patient standing comfortably, have them lift their leg to a position where their heel touches their knee. To "test" single limb support, instruct them to lift their hand from their side to up in front of their face and say the word "now." When the patient removes their hand and says, "now," the test begins.
If your patient is comfortable with this task, have them try closing their eyes (Figure 1). To make this task more functional, or if your patient is unstable, have them begin by touching their fingers to a countertop or chair, and then saying, "now." If the patient can balance, it would be easier to have the patient slowly move their hand from their side to in front of their face and say "now" (Figure 2).

for 'divided choir', is an oft-employed convention in sixteenth-century music for four, five or eight singers in which the large choir is split into two or more independent sections, thereby providing for multiple variations of similar textures and allowing the music to emerge from several places within the same space. Based on Renaissance architectural precepts, cori spezzati can be understood as the musical analogue to an interior space that is organized in multiple, differently located, levels and features. Each zone or level, as well as each perspective on a given level, is similarly constructed, having the same features, but the overall ensemble of the interior reveals the multiplicity and variety of these articulations. According to Tripp, “some of our practices are reflected in the Bio-cultural Protocols, and some are not.” Tribal leaders recognize the vital relationship between the tribe and land that can only be achieved through the integrated use of Western Science and Traditional Ecological Knowledge. Indeed, with regard to climate change, there is as much to learn from traditional practices as there is to learn from Western ecological sciences. The combined strategies outlined in the Eco-Cultural Resources Management Plan are designed to protect the Karuk cultural heritage while respecting the limits of natural ecosystems. The policy was crafted in the hopes that it would provide a model for other indigenous nations to follow.
Tripp emphasizes that historically, tribal communities have not caused the majority of climate change.
